A.explanation: Distance $p$ is between the single slit and double slit. It affects coherence and brightness but is not in the fringe spacing formula, so changing it does not change fringe spacing.

B.explanation: Distance $q$ is the double-slit separation $a$. Since fringe spacing $x$ is inversely proportional to $a$, decreasing $q$ increases $x$.

C.explanation: Distance $r$ is the double-slit to screen distance $D$. Since $x$ is directly proportional to $D$, decreasing $r$ decreases fringe spacing.

D.explanation: Fringe spacing $x$ is directly proportional to wavelength $\lambda$. Decreasing $\lambda$ decreases fringe spacing.

hints: Look at the diagram labels: $q$ is the separation of the two slits in the double slit and $r$ is the distance from the double slit to the screen.
Recall the double-slit fringe spacing relation $x = \lambda D / a$ and decide which label is $a$ and which label is $D$.
Check each change to see if it makes the numerator larger or the denominator smaller, because only larger $\lambda D$ or smaller $a$ will increase $x$.
walkthrough: Identify the quantities in the diagram: $q$ is the slit separation $a$ of the interfering sources, $r$ is the slit to screen distance $D$, and $p$ only sets up coherent illumination from the single slit.
State the governing rule for double-slit interference: fringe spacing $x = \lambda D / a$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of the light.
Substitute the apparatus labels: $x = \lambda r / q$. Distance $p$ does not appear, so changing $p$ does not change $x$.
Use proportional reasoning: $x$ increases if $\lambda$ increases, if $r$ increases, or if $q$ decreases.
Decreasing $q$ makes the denominator smaller, so $x$ becomes larger. Decreasing $r$ or decreasing $\lambda$ would make $x$ smaller. This is option B.
